"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/trionic-array-i/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

3637. Trionic Array I

You are given an integer array nums of length n.

An array is trionic if there exist indices 0 < p < q < n - 1 such that:

- nums[0...p] is strictly increasing,
- nums[p...q] is strictly decreasing,
- nums[q...n - 1] is strictly increasing.

Return true if nums is trionic, otherwise return false.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,3,5,4,2,6]
Output: true
Explanation:
Pick p = 2, q = 4:
- nums[0...2] = [1, 3, 5] is strictly increasing (1 < 3 < 5).
- nums[2...4] = [5, 4, 2] is strictly decreasing (5 > 4 > 2).
- nums[4...5] = [2, 6] is strictly increasing (2 < 6).

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,1,3]
Output: false
Explanation:
There is no way to pick p and q to form the required three segments.

Constraints:

    3 <= n <= 100
    -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000
"""


class Solution:
    def isTrionic(self, nums: List[int]) -> bool:
        n = len(nums)
        # p and q must satisfy 0 < p < q < n-1
        # So p in [1, n-3], q in [p+1, n-2]
        for p in range(1, n - 2):
            # Check strictly increasing from 0 to p
            if not all(nums[i] < nums[i + 1] for i in range(p)):
                continue
            for q in range(p + 1, n - 1):
                # Check strictly decreasing from p to q
                if not all(nums[i] > nums[i + 1] for i in range(p, q)):
                    continue
                # Check strictly increasing from q to n-1
                if all(nums[i] < nums[i + 1] for i in range(q, n - 1)):
                    return True
        return False


sol = Solution()

print(sol.isTrionic([1, 3, 5, 4, 2, 6]))  # True

assert sol.isTrionic([1, 3, 5, 4, 2, 6]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([2, 1, 3]) == False

assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) == False
assert sol.isTrionic([7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) == False
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 3]) == False
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 4]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([-3, -2, -1, -2, -3, -2, -1]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 3, 5, 4, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 1000, 999, 998, 1000]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 2, 1]) == False
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2]) == True
assert sol.isTrionic([1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0, 1]) == True
